items.title: Sumner Labat Interview, 1962-11-11
items.q: So he gave me about a dozen lessons, private you see.

ctx.x: Didn't know where I was going. Never lived in my life before. Didn't know where I was going.

What was it like up there in Virginia as far as music was concerned? Well, it was good. They had a brass band and they had an orchestra. And they had an orchestra, and I used to play second violin in the orchestra. And they had a professor from Richmond, Virginia to come up there and teach us twice a week, sometimes once a week. Well there were two of us who were playing violin in the orchestra at the time and the professor taking a light to me. And he said, boy I got music in you. And he started giving special…

There were some good musicians around in Virginia. I know that a lot of them, one fellow made a name for himself, went to New York, named Ward Pinkett but he died. I think he went to Hampton Institute. Yeah. I doubt if you'd known him, he's probably younger than you. We had an Italian professor up there, he was good. Professor Gadibasio was his name.
